summary: GVE Level 2 Result Assembly defines authoritative workflow execution records, composition-facing operation results and evidence, deterministic evidence aggregation, optional fail-closed finalization of immutable authoritative workflow-result versions, explicit result supersession and one current lineage head, truthful representation of pre-execution failure and every operation outcome, partial effects, incomplete or contradictory evidence, and complete evidence-bound traceability.

definitions.text: The application-independent result record for one declared operation, attributable to its operation identity, selected plugin, validated operation contract, lifecycle outcome, effect-state claims, dependencies, handoffs, and supporting evidence.

Evidence attributable to one operation and sufficient to support only the specific operation-level requested, authorized, attempted, completed, observed, or verified claims stated in that operation result.
Application-independent evidence that supports workflow-level composition, validation, ordering, dependency, handoff, aggregate effect-state, and result-assembly claims.

The deterministic assembly of operation evidence and workflow evidence without converting lifecycle, validation, plugin, dependency, handoff, blocked, skipped, failed, or unattempted status into an effect claim.

The immutable authoritative record of one governed workflow processing or execution identity, including planning or validation disposition, lifecycle facts, operation outcomes, evidence, uncertainty, contradictions, finalization disposition, and only the effect claims supported by evidence. It exists whether or not a workflow result can be finalized.
One uniquely identified immutable finalized authoritative workflow result in a result lineage. A correction creates a new version and never mutates an accepted historical version.

The explicit evidence-bound relationship by which a new finalized result version identifies the prior version it supersedes and states the correction reason without deleting or rewriting prior authoritative history.

The single finalized result version in one workflow-result lineage that is not superseded by another accepted version. Historical superseded versions remain authoritative records of their accepted content but are not current.

The fail-closed disposition recorded in the authoritative workflow execution record when available facts cannot produce a complete, consistent, uniquely attributable, sufficiently evidenced finalized workflow result. It is not itself a finalized workflow result.

A finalized immutable result version for one governed workflow realization. It includes the workflow and execution identities, applicable accepted or rejected plan identity, every required operation result, workflow evidence, aggregate claims, partial effects, incomplete evidence, and traceability. It exists only when result finalization succeeds.

An authoritative workflow execution record representing rejection before any operation attempt. It records the rejection cause and all identifiable operations as unattempted without claiming workflow execution, operation attempt, completion, observation, verification, or successful result finalization.

The required result representation for one declared operation, including whether it completed, failed, was blocked, was skipped, or remained otherwise unattempted, together with distinct effect-state claims and supporting evidence.

An effect supported for one or more operations or effect dimensions while the complete workflow effect is not supported. Partial effects must be explicit and must not be represented as whole-workflow completion.

A result condition in which available evidence is insufficient to support one or more otherwise possible operation-level or workflow-level claims. Absence of sufficient evidence must remain explicit and must not be converted into a positive claim.
A claim that the complete governed workflow effect finished successfully. It requires sufficient evidence for every operation and composition condition required by the accepted plan.
A claim that the relevant complete workflow effect was independently observed. It requires observation evidence covering the workflow claim and must remain distinct from completion.

A claim that the relevant complete workflow effect was verified against its governing criteria. It requires verification evidence covering the workflow claim and must remain distinct from completion and observation.

The deterministic links from every workflow-level and operation-level claim to the workflow identity, operation identity, selected plugin, validated contract, dependencies, handoffs, authority, lifecycle outcome, and supporting evidence from which the claim is derived.

The attributable result-assembly record of how each claim-relevant evidence item was classified, evaluated, admitted or rejected with reason, and considered during authoritative execution-record and workflow-result realization.

Claim-relevant evidence that is not admitted because it is malformed, stale, unauthorized, inapplicable, non-attributable, or otherwise fails a governed admission criterion. Rejection does not erase the evidence record or its attributable reason.

requirements.text: Exactly one authoritative workflow execution record must represent each governed workflow processing or execution identity, including pre-execution rejection, partial progress, failure, successful completion, and result-finalization failure.

A finalized authoritative workflow result may be produced only when finalization succeeds. Each finalized result version must represent every operation required by the applicable accepted or rejected plan exactly once and preserve each operation's identity and actual outcome.
Every operation result must be attributable to exactly one operation identity, selected plugin, validated operation contract, lifecycle outcome, and supporting operation evidence.
Requested, authorized, attempted, completed, observed, and verified must remain separate claims at both operation and workflow levels. No claim may be inferred solely from another claim.

A plugin, lifecycle, validation, dependency, handoff, blocked, skipped, failed, or unattempted status must not by itself establish that an effect was requested, authorized, attempted, completed, observed, or verified.

A pre-execution validation failure must produce a pre-execution failure record that records the rejection cause, represents every identifiable operation as unattempted, and does not claim that workflow execution or successful result finalization began.

Failed, blocked, skipped, and otherwise unattempted operations must be represented explicitly and distinctly in the authoritative workflow execution record and, when finalization succeeds, in the finalized workflow result; they must not be omitted or collapsed into a generic non-success status.

An operation may claim attempted only when evidence supports an authorized governed attempt, and may claim completed only when evidence supports successful completion of that operation's governed effect.
An operation may claim observed or verified only when distinct sufficient evidence supports the corresponding observation or verification claim; completion alone is insufficient.

Evidence aggregation must preserve the identity, scope, authority, provenance, and supported claim of each evidence item and must not broaden an operation-level claim into a workflow-level claim without sufficient support.

Partial effects must be represented explicitly with the operations and effect dimensions they cover in the authoritative workflow execution record and any finalized workflow result, and must not be represented as complete workflow success.
Incomplete evidence must be represented explicitly for every unsupported or indeterminate claim and must prevent any corresponding positive operation-level or workflow-level claim.

A workflow completion claim may be made only when every operation and composition condition required for complete workflow success is represented and supported by sufficient evidence. Partial operation success, blocked or skipped required operations, failed required operations, or incomplete evidence must prevent the claim.
A workflow observation claim may be made only when distinct sufficient observation evidence covers the complete workflow claim. Workflow completion alone must not establish observation.

A workflow verification claim may be made only when distinct sufficient verification evidence covers the complete workflow claim against its governing criteria. Completion or observation alone must not establish verification.

Every aggregate workflow claim must be traceable deterministically to the operation results and workflow evidence that support it, including relevant operation identities, selected plugins, validated contracts, dependencies, and handoffs.

Conflicting, duplicate, ambiguous, stale, unauthorized, malformed, or non-attributable operation results or evidence must fail result finalization closed, remain truthfully represented in the authoritative workflow execution record, and prevent unsupported authoritative claims.

The authoritative workflow execution record must bind one workflow identity and one governed processing or execution identity and must identify the accepted-plan identity when one exists, or the rejected planning or validation context when no plan was accepted.

When result finalization fails because evidence or result facts are incomplete, contradictory, ambiguous, stale, malformed, unauthorized, or non-attributable, the execution record must preserve that disposition and its supporting facts, and no finalized authoritative workflow result may be claimed.
Every finalized authoritative workflow result must have one stable result-version identity and must remain immutable after acceptance.

A correction must create a new finalized result version that explicitly identifies the directly superseded version, the correction reason, and the evidence basis; it must not mutate, delete, or silently replace accepted historical result content.

Each workflow-result lineage must have at most one current lineage head. Multiple immutable historical versions are permitted only through explicit acyclic supersession relationships, and every superseded version must remain attributable and inspectable as accepted history.

Lifecycle, validation, finalization, current-head, and superseded status are record or lineage facts and must not substitute for requested, authorized, attempted, completed, observed, or verified effect claims.
The core may assemble application-independent result facts and evidence obligations, but it must not interpret, normalize, override, or derive plugin-specific result meaning.

This specification must not define concrete plugin-specific result payload schemas, maintained runtime implementation, GitHub or remote-service behavior, or sibling Level 2 local-plugin-boundary responsibilities.

Evidence aggregation and result assembly must preserve an evidence disposition for every claim-relevant received evidence item, including rejected evidence and admitted evidence that is adverse, contradictory, or unresolved; no such item may disappear merely because it does not support a result claim.

Evidence admission does not imply support for a claim. Every operation- or workflow-level claim must remain traceable only to evidence that actually supports that claim, while contradictory admitted evidence and rejected evidence remain attributable and inspectable.

includes: Authoritative workflow execution records for every governed processing or execution identity
Optional fail-closed finalization of authoritative workflow-result versions
Result-version identity, immutability, explicit supersession, and one current lineage head
Failed, blocked, skipped, and unattempted operation representation
Separate requested, authorized, attempted, completed, observed, and verified claims
Partial effects, incomplete evidence, and contradictory evidence
Workflow completion, observation, and verification evidence gates
Complete result traceability and preserved historical lineage
evidence disposition, rejected-evidence preservation, and separation of admission from claim support
